ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r3.claim: The soul mirrors the larger world: God inspires good and evil, inclines it to good and against evil, and requires it to preserve balance; unchecked evil leads to arrogance and disorder.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r3.anchor: inclined it towards good and made it hate evil

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r1.claim: The soul itself witnesses its Maker’s purpose: awareness of good and evil entails adopting good and avoiding evil; success is purification and failure is sin, so denying accountability contradicts this witness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r1.anchor: the awareness of good and evil is found in it. Obviously, the reason for giving him this awareness is that man should adopt good and shield himself from evil

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r4.claim: Taswiyah denotes creation’s final stage, as in 87:2; the perfected soul’s capacities make it a witness that humans have responsibilities and answer to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r4.anchor: here it is not merely the initial stage of the creation of the human soul which is referred to in this oath, its final stage is also in consideration

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r4.claim: Using every divine favour rightly serves one’s own interest and expresses gratitude; failing to do so is self-destruction.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r4.anchor: every favour God has bestowed on him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r5.claim: As a person who closes his eyes risks falling and bears responsibility, a person must stay alert to the moral path he follows.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r5.anchor: there is a strong probability that he might fall in a pit and he himself would be responsible for this mishap and no other person.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r3.claim: Suppressing the complement lets everything evident from the oaths count as its content; one prominent implication is that God destroys rebellious nations.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r3.anchor: The benefit of this suppression is that everything

QUSHAYRI:v3p424/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p424/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p424/r4.claim: God inspires the soul with wickedness and piety by abandoning or enabling it; another view takes them as the paths of good and evil.
QUSHAYRI:v3p424/r4.anchor: فجورها : حركتها في طلب الرزق ، وتقواها : سكونها بحكم القدير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī rejects the infinitive reading because of فألهمها and prefers a relative meaning like the powerful builder and wise maker.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r8.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: جعلت مصدرية، وليس بالوجه لقوله: فألهمها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r9.claim: The author replies that an infinitive mā is sound: the pronoun in فألهمها can return to God understood from context, and no syntactic corruption follows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r9.anchor: ولا يلزم ذلك لأنا إذا جعلناها مصدرية عاد الضمير على ما يفهم من سياق الكلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r3.claim: The mention of taqwā is followed by success for the one who purifies himself, and failure is followed by mention of the people of Paradise as a counterpoint.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r3.anchor: وحين قال: وتقواها أعقبه بقوله: قد أفلح من زكاها.

FARRA:v3p266/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p266/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p266/r6.claim: God made the soul know the path of good and evil, as in the verse about showing the two paths.
FARRA:v3p266/r6.anchor: وقوله عز وجل: فألهمها فجورها وتقواها (8) عرفها سبيل الخير، وسبيل الشر، وهو مثل قوله: «وهديناه النجدين » .

NAHHAS:v5p235/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p235/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p235/r9.anchor:
مفعولان
9 روى ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p527/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p527/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p527/r9.claim: In another report the moon follows the day, what the earth contains is what God created in it, and inspiration teaches obedience and disobedience.
DURR-FULL:v8p527/r9.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير من طريق العوفي عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p527/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p527/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p527/r12.claim: He said God divided the earth and made known to the soul its good and evil.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r6.claim: Mujahid says the soul was shown its wickedness.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r6.anchor: فالهمها فجورها وتقواها قال : عرفها شقاءها

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r14.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r14.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r14.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says God bound the soul to its wickedness and its piety.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r14.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير فالهمها قال : الزمها فجورها وتقواها

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r15.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r15.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r15.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses the soul's wickedness and piety as disobedience and obedience.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r15.anchor: عن الضحاك فالهمها فجورها وتقواها قال : الطاعة والمعصية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p366/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p366/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p366/r4.claim: The oath is prepared by noting that purifying the soul leads to success, while neglecting its reform leads to immorality and loss.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p366/r4.anchor: ومهد لذلك بالتنبيه على أن تزكية النفس سبب الفلاح ، وأن التقصير في إصلاحها سبب الفجور والخسران .

JISHUMI:v10p7429/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7429/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7429/r7.claim: He says ilhām and iltihām are equivalent; related terms mean informing, imparting, suggesting, or teaching.
JISHUMI:v10p7429/r7.anchor: قال أبو مسلم: الإلهام والالتهام بمعنى، وسواء قولك: الإلهام والإلقاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r8.claim: Inspiring vice and piety means making their difference clear and enabling choice; the following verses show the human being performs purification or defilement, which respectively elevate through piety or diminish through sin.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r8.anchor: ومعنى إلهام الفجور والتقوى : إفهامهما وإعقالهما ، وأن أحدهما حسن والآخر قبيح

RAZI-FULL:v31p171/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p171/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p171/r1.claim: The sura urges obedience and warns against disobedience; oaths by beneficial created things prompt reflection and gratitude because divine oaths weigh heavily on the heart.
RAZI-FULL:v31p171/r1.anchor: المقصود من هذه السورة الترغيب في الطاعات والتحذير من المعاصي

RAZI-FULL:v31p171/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p171/r3.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v31p171/r3.claim: Al-Qadi denies that 'what made it' refers to God: the oath cannot put another beside God's own oath, and the phrase should mean the heaven and its building; al-Zamakhshari objects that this disrupts the syntax with 'inspired it.'
RAZI-FULL:v31p171/r3.anchor: وهو أن { ما } مع ما بعده في حكم المصدر

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:anmerkung/r1.claim: Qur'anic oaths probably draw on a characteristic expression of pre-Islamic soothsayers, though the connection remains insufficiently researched.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zu grundsätzlichen Hinweisen zu den koranischen Schwüren sowie ihrer wahrscheinlichen, aber bis dato noch nicht hinreichend untersuchten Anlehnung an ein charakteristisches Ausdrucksmittel altarabischer Seher

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:anmerkung/r2.claim: The structure and function of cumulative oath series are discussed at 93:1–2, with many parallels.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Zu Aufbau und Funktion ‚akkumulativer Schwurserien’ wie dem vorliegenden Passus s. die Anmerkung zu 93:1.2 mit zahlreichen Parallelstellen

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r1.claim: An eight-verse oath series leads into the antithetical statement in verses 9–10; the pre-Islamic genre is repurposed in verses 5–7 to express biblical creation ideas.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r1.anchor: mit anschließender, antithetischer Schwuraussage (V. 9.10). Die Schwurserie

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r2.claim: The series moves through three complementary or contrasting pairs—sun/moon, night/day, heaven/earth—then the soul, whose opposed moral capacities are specified in verse 8.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r2.anchor: drei aus kontrastierenden bzw. komplementären Elementen aufgebaute Paare (V. 1.2: Sonne und Mond, V. 3.4: Nacht und Tag, V. 5.6: Himmel und Erde)

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r3.claim: The text leaves open whether God instills sin and piety deterministically or presents the human being with a choice, but embeds moral opposition within creation's binary order.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r3.anchor: Ob das „Eingeben“ von Sünde und Gottesfurcht deterministisch zu verstehen ist oder meint, dass Gott den Menschen vor die Wahl zwischen beiden Polen stellt, macht der Text selbst nicht deutlich

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r4.claim: The oath series narrows from cosmic creation, traced vertically from celestial bodies to earth, to the human moral subject.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r4.anchor: Zum einen verengt die Serie sukzessive den Fokus von der kosmischen Schöpfungsordnung (die vertikal, von Himmelskörpern bis zur Erde, durchlaufen wird) auf das moralische Subjekt des Menschen

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r5.claim: Its shift from creation to humanity resembles the 81:1–14 sequence, which evokes the world's eschatological dissolution rather than cyclical operation.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r5.anchor: Eine ähnliche Struktur weist etwa auch die ʾiḏā-Serie 81:1–14 auf, wo allerdings die eschatologische Auflösung der Schöpfung und nicht wie in Q 91 ihr zyklisches Funktionieren evoziert wird

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r6.claim: A caesura after verse 4 divides effects and activities of the oath's objects in verses 1–4 from references to God's creating activity in verses 5–8.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r6.anchor: Zum anderen besitzt die Serie eine deutliche Binnenzäsur nach V. 4, die eine Untergliederung in zwei Gesätze nahelegt

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r7.claim: The creator first emerges through indirect, enigmatic mā in the second half of the series; the explicit naming of the Lord in verse 14 resolves the suspense.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r7.anchor: Das dadurch aufgebaute Spannungsmoment löst im Grunde erst die explizite Nennung des „Herrn“ in V. 14 auf

TABATABAI:91:1-15/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:1-15/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:91:1-15/r3.claim: Zurarah, Humran, and Muhammad ibn Muslim report from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq that God showed the soul what it should do and leave.
TABATABAI:91:1-15/r3.anchor: روى زرارة وحمران ومحمد بن مسلم عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله عليهما السلام

TABRISI:91:1-15/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:1-15/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:91:1-15/r15.claim: Inspiration means making the paths of sin and piety known, inclining people away from sin and toward piety.
TABRISI:91:1-15/r15.anchor: أي عرفها طريق الفجور والتقوى وزهدها في الفجور ورغبها في التقوى عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:91:1-15/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:1-15/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:91:1-15/r16.claim: Alternatively, God taught the soul obedience and disobedience so it could choose good and avoid evil.
TABRISI:91:1-15/r16.anchor: علمها الطاعة والمعصية لتفعل الطاعة وتذر المعصية وتجتني الخير

THALABI:v10p212#3/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p212#3/r13.speaker: ابن عباس برواية الوالبي
THALABI:v10p212#3/r13.claim: He says God made good and evil clear to the soul.
THALABI:v10p212#3/r13.anchor: قال ابن عباس برواية الوالبي: يبين لها الخير والشر

THALABI:v10p212#3/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p212#3/r14.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p212#3/r14.claim: He says God taught the soul obedience and disobedience.
THALABI:v10p212#3/r14.anchor: وقال العوفي عنه: علمها الطاعة والمعصية

THALABI:v10p212#3/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p212#3/r15.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v10p212#3/r15.claim: He says God taught the soul what actions it should and should not do.
THALABI:v10p212#3/r15.anchor: الكلبي: أعلمها ما يأتي وما ينبغي

THALABI:v10p212#3/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p212#3/r16.speaker: ابن زيد وابن الفضل
THALABI:v10p212#3/r16.claim: They say God placed the capacity for these paths in the soul: granting success for reverence and abandoning it toward wickedness.
THALABI:v10p212#3/r16.anchor: وقال ابن زيد وابن الفضل: جعل فيها ذلك يعني بتوفيقه إياها للتقوى وخذلانه إياها للفجور

THALABI:v10p212#3/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p212#3/r17.speaker: أبو الأسود الدؤلي عن عمران بن حصين
THALABI:v10p212#3/r17.claim: Imran asks whether people's actions are predetermined or arise from prophetic instruction and proof. Abu al-Aswad answers that all is decreed, adding that God created and owns everything and is not questioned while people are.
THALABI:v10p212#3/r17.anchor: عن أبي الأسود الدؤلي قال ب قال لي عمران بن حصين: أرأيت ما يعمل فيه الناس ويتكادحون فيه؟ أشيء قضى عليهم ومضى عليهم من قدر سبق

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:1-8/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:1-8/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:1-8/r6.claim: God taught the soul obedience and disobedience.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:1-8/r6.anchor: { فألهمها فجورها وتقواها } علمها الطاعة والمعصية

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r6.claim: Fujur means all evil, sin, and deviation; taqwa here means uprightness, goodness, and steadfastness on the right path.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r6.anchor: fücûr her türlü kötülüğü, günah ve sapmayı; âyette fücûrun karşıtı olarak kullanılan takvâ ise burada doğruluk, iyilik

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r7.claim: Ilham here is God's placing in human nature an innate capacity and freedom to recognize and distinguish right from wrong, good from evil, and choose between them before learning or experience.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r7.anchor: Allah Teâlâ’nın insanın fıtratına doğru ve yanlışı, iyilik ve kötülüğü, günah ve sevabı bilme, tanıma, ayırt etme

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r8.claim: Verses 7–8 summarize humans as morally dual beings created able to choose good or evil, with salvation or ruin depending on that choice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r8.anchor: insanın ahlâkî bakımdan çift kutuplu bir varlık olduğunu, iyilik veya kötülük yollarından dilediğini seçebilecek bir tabiatta yaratıldığını

BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r2.claim: The ف in فألهمها may express causation after the soul's formation or sequence after its outward and inward faculties were completed.
BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r2.anchor: الفاء إن كانت لسببية التسوية فالأمر ظاهر وإن كانت لتقبها فلعل المراد منها

BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r3.claim: Inspiration is a thought placed in the heart from God or the highest realm; its root conveys swallowing something.
BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r3.anchor: والإلهام القاء الشيء في الروع إما من جهة الله أو من جهة الملاء الأعلى

BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r4.claim: Fujur breaches religion's veil; it precedes taqwa for the verse's rhyme or because suppressing sin is especially urgent, and the soul can choose either path.
BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r4.anchor: والفجور شق ستر الديانة قدم على التقوى لمراعاة الفواصل أو لشدة الاهتمام

BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r5.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r5.claim: Some elders say inspiration is only for good: the soul is shown sin to avoid and piety to practice, since God never commands evil.
BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r5.anchor: قال بعض الكبار الإلهام لا يكون إلا في الخير فلا يقال في الشر الهمني الله

BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r6.claim: The form انبعث responds to بعث, as in saying that someone was urged toward a matter and responded.
BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لا يخفى إن محل الإلهام هو النفس

BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r7.claim: Another explanation says permissible acts are not inspired because they belong to the soul by nature from the moment it is created.
BURSEVI:v10p342#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم لم ينسب سبحانه إلى النفس خاطر المباح ولا إلهامه فيها

QASHANI:91:8/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:91:8/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:91:8/r4.claim: God made the soul know wickedness and godfearing through angelic prompting and the material intellect’s capacity to recognize the good of piety and evil of sin.
QASHANI:91:8/r4.anchor: أفهمها إياهما وأشعرها بهما بالإلقاء الملكي والتمكين من معرفتهما وحسن التقوى وقبح الفجور

SULAMI:v2p397/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p397/r1.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v2p397/r1.claim: God inspires the people destined for felicity with piety and those destined for misery with wickedness.
SULAMI:v2p397/r1.anchor: قال القاسم : ألهم أهل السعادة التقوى ، واهل الشقاوة الفجور

SULAMI:v2p397/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p397/r2.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v2p397/r2.claim: Fujur can mean exertion in earning livelihood, while taqwa is a heart made still by trust in God's promise of provision.
SULAMI:v2p397/r2.anchor: وقال أيضا : الهمها فجورها . أي تعبها وكسبها في طلب الرزق

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3436#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3436#3/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3436#3/r1.claim: The Prophet says people's deeds are already decreed, yet they work because each person is prepared for the destination for which God created him; he cites the soul and its inspiration toward wickedness and piety.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3436#3/r1.anchor: عن عمران بن حصين : ' ان رجلا قال يا رسول الله : ارايت ما يعمل الناس اليوم ويكدحون فيه شيء قد قضى عليهم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3436#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3436#3/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3436#3/r2.claim: The Prophet recited the verse and prayed for a soul's piety and purification, saying God is the best purifier and its guardian and master.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3436#3/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرا : فالهمها فجوها وتقواها قال : اللهم ات نفسي تقواها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r1.claim: The clause about inspiration is coordinated with the soul's fashioning, and its fa signals that inspiration arises from that fashioning; the pronoun may refer to the act of straightening.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r1.anchor: وعطف بالفاء لأن الإلهام ناشىء عن التسوية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r2.claim: Alternatively, mā may be relative and refer to God's act: building the sky, spreading the earth and straightening the soul.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون { ما } موصولة صادقة على فعل الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r3.claim: Soul's physical and mental capacities are adjusted from completion of embryonic formation and early childhood, then develop in quality until inspiration occurs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r3.anchor: فالتسوية حاصلة من وقت تمام خلقة الجنين من أول أطوار الصبا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r4.claim: Ilhām is a verbal noun of alhama; the simple verb is obsolete, the noun is rare, and lexicographers cited no Arabic poetic evidence for it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r4.anchor: مصدر ألهم ، وهو فعل متعد بالهمزة ولكن المجرد منه ممات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r5.claim: In its specialized sense, ilhām is knowledge arriving in the soul without teaching, experience or thought, whether innate and necessary or reached through evidence and reasoning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r5.anchor: ويطلق الإلهام إطلاقا خاصا على حدوث علم في النفس بدون تعليم ولا تجربة ولا تفكير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r6.speaker: الراغب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r6.claim: Al-Rāghib defines ilhām as placing something in the heart and limits it to what comes from God or the higher angelic realm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r6.anchor: قال الراغب : الإلهام : إيقاع الشيء في الروع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r7.claim: The Quran may have coined this precise psychological term or revived it; its root conveys gulping, while Sufis use it technically for unsupported knowledge.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r7.anchor: ولذلك فهذا اللفظ إن لم يكن من مبتكرات القرآن يكن مما أحياه القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r8.claim: Here the soul's constitution produces primary and necessary cognition, instincts such as a baby's first search for the breast or avoidance of harm, and eventually the beginnings of rational acquisition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p369/r8.anchor: ابتداء من الانسياق الجبلي نحو الأمور النافعة كطلب الرضيع الثدي أول مرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r1.claim: Innate discernment makes the divinely revealed distinction between transgression and piety intelligible; without minds, people could not grasp commands, punishment or reward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r1.anchor: فلولا العقول لما تيسر إفهام الإنسان الفجور والتقوى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r2.claim: Fujūr precedes taqwā because the surah addresses polytheists, whose deeds were mostly transgression, while Muslims were then few.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r2.anchor: وتقديم الفجور على التقوى مراعى فيه أحوال المخاطبين بهذه السورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r3.claim: The masculine form alhamahā treats the verbal noun taswiyah as nonfeminine or follows the masculine form of mā if it is relative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r3.anchor: ومجيء فعل : ( ألهمها ) بصيغة الإسناد إلى ضمير مذكر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r7.claim: God showed the soul the paths of sin and piety and gave it the capacity to acquire either.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r7.anchor: ومعنى قوله تعالى: فجورها وتقواها أي عرفها طرق ذلك وجعل لها قوة يصح معها اكتساب الفجور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p140/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p140/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p140/r1.claim: Ilhām is placing something in the soul.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p140/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p140/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p140/r2.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says God made the soul's wickedness and piety binding upon it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p140/r2.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير ألزمها فجورها وتقواها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p140/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p140/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p140/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says God placed both within it by granting success toward piety and withholding aid toward wickedness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p140/r3.anchor: وقال ابن زيد جعل ذلك فيها بتوفيقه إياها للتقوى وخذلانه إياها للفجور

IBNKATHIR:91:8/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:8/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:91:8/r1.claim: God inspired the soul to its wickedness and piety by showing both and guiding it toward what He decreed for it.
IBNKATHIR:91:8/r1.anchor: أي : فأرشدها إلى فجورها وتقواها ،   أي : بين لها ذلك ،   وهداها إلى ما قدر لها .

IBNKATHIR:91:8/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:8/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:91:8/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and al-Thawri say God made good and evil clear to the soul.
IBNKATHIR:91:8/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : { فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَاهَا } بين لها الخير والشر .   وكذا قال مجاهد ،   وقتادة ،   والضحاك ،   والثوري .

IBNKATHIR:91:8/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:8/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR:91:8/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says God inspired the soul with good and evil.
IBNKATHIR:91:8/r3.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير : ألهمها الخير والشر .   وقال ابن زيد : جعل فيها فجورها وتقواها .

IBNKATHIR:91:8/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:8/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR:91:8/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says God placed the soul's wickedness and piety within it.
IBNKATHIR:91:8/r4.anchor: قال : ففيم نعمل ؟ قال :  " من كان الله خلقه لإحدى المنزلتين يُهَيِّئه لها ،

IBNKATHIR:91:8/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:8/r5.speaker: عمران بن حصين
IBNKATHIR:91:8/r5.claim: In a report carried by Abu al-Aswad al-Duʾali, ʿImran ibn Husayn asks whether people's strenuous deeds are fixed by prior decree or left to what the Prophet brings with proof; the Prophet answers that they have been decreed and that God prepares each person for the station for which He created him, citing these verses. Ahmad and Muslim transmit the report.
IBNKATHIR:91:8/r5.anchor: قال :  " بل شيء قد قضي{[30133]}  عليهم "  .   قال : ففيم نعمل ؟ قال :  " من كان الله خلقه لإحدى المنزلتين يُهَيِّئه لها ،

IBNKATHIR:91:10/r12.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR:91:10/r12.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet reciting the verse and praying that God give his soul piety and purify it; Ibn Kathir notes this route is not included by the major collectors.
IBNKATHIR:91:10/r12.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ : { فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَاهَا } قال :  " اللهم آت نفسي تقواها ،

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p529#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p529#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p529#6/r1.claim: God made the soul aware of its wickedness and piety by its innate nature.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p529#6/r1.anchor: {فألهمها فجورها وتقواها} أي عرفها (5) في الفطرة.

JISHUMI:v10p7431/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r21.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة وسفيان والضحاك
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r21.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Qatāda, Sufyān, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say God inspired the soul by clarifying and teaching it wickedness and reverence.
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r21.anchor: أي: بين لها الخير والشر، وعرفها الفجور والتقوى، عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد

JISHUMI:v10p7431/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r22.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r22.claim: Abū Muslim connects the fāʾ of “inspired it” to “the soul and what shaped it,” meaning God shaped the soul and then inspired it.
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r22.anchor: والفاء في قوله: فألهمها عطف على قوله: (ونفس وما سواها)

KASHSHAF:91:8/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:8/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:8/r1.claim: Inspiring vice and piety means making both understandable, showing one good and the other bad, and enabling a choice; the following verses show that people enact either path.
KASHSHAF:91:8/r1.anchor: إفهامهما وإعقالهما ،   وأنّ أحدهما حسن والآخر قبيح

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r14.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r14.claim: He interprets alhamaha as making the soul know its choices.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r15.speaker: ابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r15.claim: He interprets alhamaha as compelling or binding the soul to its course.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r16.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r16.claim: He interprets its wickedness and piety as misery and happiness.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r17.claim: He interprets them as evil and good.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r18.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r18.claim: He interprets them as obedience and disobedience.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r19.claim: A further possibility is that fear and hope are the motives that lead to wickedness and piety.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r20.speaker: جوبير عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r20.claim: They transmit that when the Prophet recited this verse, he raised his voice in prayer asking God to grant his soul piety and purify it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r20.anchor: جوبير عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس

MUJAHID:v2p763#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p763#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MUJAHID:v2p763#2/r1.claim: Sa‘id ibn Jubayr says the soul was made to adhere to both wickedness and piety.
MUJAHID:v2p763#2/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ﴿ فألهمها فجورها وتقواها ﴾ قال ألزمها الفجور والتقوى

MUJAHID:v2p763#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p763#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p763#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says God made the soul know misery and happiness.
MUJAHID:v2p763#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد قال عرفها الشقاء والسعادة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#2/r1.claim: God made the soul understand obedience and disobedience and recognize that one is good and the other bad.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#2/r1.anchor: فأعلمها طاعتها ومعصيتها أى أفهمها أن أحدهما حسن والآخر قبيح

QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r1.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r1.claim: Mujahid, through Ibn Abi Najih, says God taught the soul or showed it the paths of wickedness and piety; Ibn Abbas agrees.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r1.anchor: أي عرفها كذا روى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد. أي عرفها طريق الفجور والتقوى وقاله ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r2.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r2.claim: Mujahid also glosses the terms as obedience and disobedience.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r2.anchor: وعن مجاهد أيضا: عرفها الطاعة والمعصية

QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Kab says God inspires a person with good and he acts on it, or inspires evil and he acts on it, according to what God wills.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r3.anchor: وعن محمد بن كعب قال: إذا أراد الله عز وجل بعبده خيرا، ألهمه الخير فعمل به

QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r4.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r4.claim: Al-Farra says God showed the two paths of good and evil, as at 90:10.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء: «فألهمها» قال: عرفها طريق الخير وطريق الشر

QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r5.speaker: الضحاك، ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits Ibn Abbas’s explanation that God inspires the pious believer with piety and the sinner with wickedness.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r5.anchor: وروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال: ألهم المؤمن المتقي تقواه، وألهم الفاجر فجوره

QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r6.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r6.claim: Qatada says God made the soul’s wickedness and piety clear to it.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r6.anchor: وعن سعيد عن قتادة قال: بين لها فجورها وتقواها

QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r7.claim: Al-Qurtubi says these explanations are close in meaning.

QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r8.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet recited the verse and prayed for his soul’s piety and purification, naming God its guardian and master.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r8.anchor:
وروي عن أبي هريرة قال:
" قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم { فألهمها فجورها وتقواها } قال: «اللهم آت نفسي تقواها، وزكها

QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r9.speaker: جويبر، الضحاك، ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r9.claim: Juwair transmits from al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet recited the verse loudly and prayed for his soul’s piety and purification.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r9.anchor:
ورواه جويبر عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس:
" أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأ هذه الآية { فألهمها فجورها وتقواها } رفع صوته بها

QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r10.speaker: عمران بن حصين
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r10.claim: In Muslim’s report, Imran ibn Husayn asks Abu al-Aswad whether human deeds were predetermined; Abu al-Aswad answers yes and says God is not questioned for what He does.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r10.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم: عن أبي الأسود الدؤلي قال: قال لي عمران بن حصين: أرأيت ما يعمل الناس اليوم، ويكدحون فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r11.speaker: رجلان من مزينة
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r11.claim: Two men of Muzayna ask the Prophet whether deeds are foreordained or proof follows the message; he says they were foreordained and cites this verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r11.anchor: إن رجلين من مزينة أتيا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالا: يا رسول الله، أرأيت ما يعمل الناس اليوم ويكدحون فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r12.claim: The Prophetic answer is that deeds were decreed beforehand, confirmed by the soul and its inspiration to wickedness and piety.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8/r12.anchor: فقال: «لا بل شيء قضي عليهم ومضى فيهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:91:8#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8#2/r1.claim: Fujur and taqwa are verbal nouns functioning as objects.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:8#2/r1.anchor: والفجور والتقوى: مصدران في موضع المفعول به

QUTB-ZILAL:91:8/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:91:8/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:91:8/r1.claim: Evil and piety are innate latent dispositions; revelation and outside influences awaken, strengthen, and direct them rather than creating them. The Qur'an also describes this as guidance along the two paths.
QUTB-ZILAL:91:8/r1.anchor: والرسالات والتوجيهات والعوامل الخارجية إنما توقظ هذه الاستعدادات وتشحذها وتوجهها هنا أو هناك

RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r1.claim: One interpretation says God made the soul understand good and evil, know one as good and the other as bad, and choose; this matches Muʿtazili doctrine and is attributed to Ibn Abbas and senior exegetes.
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r1.anchor: أن إلهام الفجور والتقوى ، إفهامها وإعقالهما

RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr glosses God's inspiration as imposing wickedness and piety on the soul.
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r2.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير : ألزمها فجورها وتقواها

RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says God put this in the soul by granting success to piety or abandoning it to wickedness.
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r3.anchor: وقال ابن زيد : جعل فيها ذلك بتوفيقه إياها للتقوى

RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r4.speaker: الزجاج والواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj and al-Wahidi prefer the second interpretation: inspiration differs from teaching or explanation and means God places something in the heart, committing the person to it.

RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r5.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r5.claim: Al-Wahidi derives inspiration from a root meaning to swallow or take in, then its use for what God casts into the heart; Ibn Zayd's reading best fits that origin.
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r5.anchor: وأصل معنى الإلهام من قولهم : لهم الشيء ، والتهمه إذا ابتلعه

RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r7.claim: Razi rejects the Muʿtazili reading: after showing God directs the cosmos, the verse says even voluntary acts fall under His decree.
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r7.anchor: فههنا لم يبق شيء مما في عالم المحسوسات

RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r8.claim: Choices cannot arise without a maker, since that makes a created event uncaused; if the servant makes them, regress follows, so their cause is God.
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r8.anchor: فحصولها إن كان لا عن فاعل فقد استغنى المحدث عن الفاعل

RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r9.claim: Razi appeals to experience: an image may suddenly enter an inattentive mind, produce desire, then bodily movement, showing inspiration as divine enabling or abandonment.
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r9.anchor: فإنه ربما كان الإنسان غافلا عن شيء فتقع صورته في قلبه دفعة

STUDYQURAN:91:8/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:8/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:91:8/r1.claim: The verse can mean God taught the soul good and evil and set its course; alternatively, He instilled iniquity and reverence in it.
STUDYQURAN:91:8/r1.anchor: As translated, this verse indicates that God taught the soul the nature of evil and good

STUDYQURAN:91:8/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:8/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:91:8/r2.claim: Both readings indicate God's instilling moral knowledge in every soul even before prophetic revelation; souls know right, wrong, their relation to God, and the primordial covenant.
STUDYQURAN:91:8/r2.anchor: it can be taken as a reference to God’s instillation of the knowledge of good and evil in every human soul

STUDYQURAN:91:8/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:8/r3.speaker: most Ashʿarite theologians
STUDYQURAN:91:8/r3.claim: Another interpretation, preferred by most Ashʿarite theologians, is that God decrees all things for each human being.
STUDYQURAN:91:8/r3.anchor: These verses can also be read as an indication that God decrees all things for each human being

STUDYQURAN:91:8/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:8/r4.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:91:8/r4.claim: In a report, the Prophet says human actions and struggles are ordained; God makes easy the path to Paradise or Hell for those created for either destination.
STUDYQURAN:91:8/r4.anchor: So the man said, “Then what is the point of our actions?” The Prophet replied

STUDYQURAN:91:8/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:8/r5.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:91:8/r5.claim: When reciting the surah, the Prophet reportedly paused here to pray that God grant the soul reverence and purify it.
STUDYQURAN:91:8/r5.anchor: when reciting this sūrah, the Prophet would stop at this verse and pray

TAB-FULL:v24p441/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p441/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p441/r1.claim: God enabled the soul to recognize what it should do or leave, whether good or evil, obedience or sin.
TAB-FULL:v24p441/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {فألهمها فجورها وتقواها} [الشمس: 8] فبين لها فجورها وتقواها

TAB-FULL:v24p441/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p441/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p441/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God made good and evil clear to the soul and taught it obedience and disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v24p441/r2.anchor: عن علي عن ابن عباس قوله: {فألهمها فجورها وتقواها} [الشمس: 8] يقول: بين الخير والشر

TAB-FULL:v24p441/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p441/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p441/r3.claim: Mujāhid says God made the soul recognize its wickedness and piety.
TAB-FULL:v24p441/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، {فألهمها فجورها وتقواها} [الشمس: 8] قال: عرفها

TAB-FULL:v24p441/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p441/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p441/r4.claim: Qatāda says God made the soul's wickedness and piety clear.
TAB-FULL:v24p441/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، {فألهمها فجورها وتقواها} [الشمس: 8] فبين لها فجورها وتقواها

TAB-FULL:v24p441/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p441/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p441/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses the phrase as distinguishing obedience from disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v24p441/r5.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {فألهمها فجورها وتقواها} [الشمس: 8] بين لها الطاعة والمعصية

TAB-FULL:v24p441/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p441/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p441/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd offers a different explanation: God placed both wickedness and piety within the soul.
TAB-FULL:v24p441/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {فألهمها فجورها وتقواها} [الشمس: 8] قال: جعل فيها فجورها وتقواها

TAB-FULL:v24p441/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p441/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p441/r7.claim: Ṭabarī cites a Prophetic report that prior decree assigns each person an abode and God prepares that person for it, using this verse as confirmation.
TAB-FULL:v24p441/r7.anchor: قال: " من كان الله خلقه لإحدى المنزلتين يهيئه لها، وتصديق ذلك في كتاب الله: {ونفس وما سواها

TABATABAI:91:9-10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r1.claim: The soul means human souls generally, not Adam’s soul alone; a specific reading does not fit the following purification and corruption language, and there is no reason to narrow the scope.
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r1.anchor: وقيل المراد بها نفس آدم عليه السلام ولا يلائمه السياق وخاصة قوله { قد أفلح من زكاها وقد خاب من دساها }

TABATABAI:91:9-10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r2.speaker: الرواية
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r2.claim: A report glosses taqwā as abstaining from what God has prohibited.
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r2.anchor: وقد فسرت في الرواية بأنها الورع عن محارم الله

TABATABAI:91:9-10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r3.claim: Fujūr means tearing the veil of religion by violating a prohibition; taqwā means shielding oneself from what is feared, here by avoiding transgression.
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r3.anchor: الفجور - على ما ذكره الراغب - شق ستر الديانة فالنهي الإلهي عن فعل أو عن ترك حجاب مضروب دونه

TABATABAI:91:9-10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r4.claim: Ilhām is casting something into the heart: God gives the soul practical images, thoughts, or judgments that identify its own actions as transgression or piety beyond the action’s shared basic category.
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r4.anchor: والإلهام الإلقاء في الروع وهو إفاضته تعالى الصور العملية من تصور أو تصديق على النفس

TABATABAI:91:9-10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r5.claim: Practical moral discernment completes the soul’s created balance and belongs to its nature, corresponding to humanity’s innate, upright disposition toward religion.
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r5.anchor: وتفريع الإلهام على التسوية في قوله { وما سواها فألهمها } الخ للاشارة إلى أن إلهام الفجور

TABATABAI:91:9-10/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r6.claim: The soul’s moral accountability includes human and jinn souls, since the Qurʾān presents jinn as responsible for faith and righteous action.
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r6.anchor: وهي النفس الانسانية ونفوس الجن على ما يظهر من الكتاب العزيز من كونهم مكلفين بالإيمان والعمل الصالح

ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r1.claim: One interpretation says God taught the soul the paths of sin and guidance.
ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r1.anchor: قيل علمها طريق الفجور وطريق الهدى

ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r2.claim: The author prefers that inspiring the soul to piety means granting it success, while inspiring it to sin means abandoning it to failure.
ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r2.anchor: والكلام على أن ألهمها التقوى، وفقها للتقوى، وألهمها فجورها خذلها، والله أعلم.

THALABI:v10p213/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p213/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p213/r11.claim: God creates each person for one of two final destinations and prepares that person for it, as the following verses affirm.
THALABI:v10p213/r11.anchor: من كان الله سبحانه خلقه لإحدى المنزلتين يهيئه الله لها وتصديق ذلك في كتاب الله عز وجل

ASAD-NOTES:91:5#n6/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:91:5#n6/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:91:5#n6/r1.claim: Humans can rise spiritually or sink into immorality; this polarity is essential to human nature and gives right choices value through moral free will.
ASAD-NOTES:91:5#n6/r1.anchor: it is this inherent polarity of tendencies which gives to every "right" choice a value

WAHIDI-QT:91:8/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:91:8/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:91:8/r1.claim: God taught the soul both obedience and disobedience.
WAHIDI-QT:91:8/r1.anchor: { فألهمها فجورها وتقواها } علمها الطاعة والمعصية

ELMALILI:91:5-10/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r14.claim: Although the infinitive reading can coordinate inspiration and avoids al-Zamakhshari's objection, it leaves the verbs' agents unstated; the relative reading identifies the Maker, suits the syntax, and is preferred.
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r14.anchor: مَا’nın mevsul olması daha zâhir ve nazımda daha âhenklidir.

ELMALILI:91:5-10/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r16.claim: Elmalılı chooses the relative reading in the translation while also signaling the infinitive reading in commentary; the oath moves from cosmic evidence to God's creation and inspiration of the soul.
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r16.anchor: mealde mevsûlü tercih ederek tefsirde masdariyyeye dahi işaret eyledik.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r1.claim: Ilham originally means swallowing something at once, then came to mean casting or instilling a meaning into the heart.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r1.anchor: bir şeyi bir defada yutmak mânasına “lehm”den if‘âl olup lahzada yutturmak mânasınadır.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r2.claim: Fujur is turning away from right and breaking its order into disobedience, and can specifically mean adultery, lying, indecency, or sinful acts; taqwa is its opposite, protecting the soul under God's care through good obedience.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r2.anchor: haktan udûl etmek, hak yolunu yarıp nizâmından çıkarak fısk u isyâna düşmektir.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r3.claim: Inspiring both does not command both; God makes a soul recognize evil as harmful and taqwa as good, commanding avoidance of evil and action for good.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r3.anchor: asıl mâna fücûrun fücur, yani nefse zarar, bozukluk; takvânın takvâ, yani nefsi koruma, iyi olduğunu duyurmak

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r4.claim: Because taqwa is a noun of result rather than a mere verbal noun, fujur likewise names sinful acts rather than the act of committing them; their meanings imply prohibition and command.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r4.anchor: mefhûmu zemmi ve binâen‘aleyh nehyi, “takvâ” mefhûmu da medhi ve binâen‘aleyh emri

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r5.claim: God gives every soul an innate general sense of benefit and harm, so people seek gain and avoid danger, though reason alone cannot always know long-term outcomes.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r5.anchor: Şüphe yok ki Allah teâlâ her nefse bir iyilik, kötülük, kâr ve zarar duygusu vermiştir.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r6.claim: Knowledge of outcomes beyond one lifetime requires revelation to holy inspired souls or accumulated experience passed across generations.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r6.anchor: Bunlar nüfûs-i mülheme-i kudsiyeye vahiy ile veya asırlarca tecribe ile bilinir.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r7.claim: Many judge good only by immediate personal pleasure, ignore others' harm and ultimate truth, disbelieve in the future, pursue quick gain, and avoid present effort for good.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r7.anchor: ilerisine inanmaz da birçok fenalıkları mücerred kendisine bugün için bir zevk

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r8.claim: A just person considers others, consults knowledgeable people, and when uncertain attends to conscience rather than immediate pleasure; God then inspires recognition of evil or good as unease or tranquility.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r8.anchor: Hak teâlâ onun kalbine onun fücur mu veya takvâ mı olduğunu ilham eyler, duyurur.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r9.claim: A Prophetic report says to consult one's heart even if jurists give a ruling, and another says to leave what causes doubt for what does not.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r9.anchor: “kalbine danış müftüler sana fetva verseler bile”

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r10.claim: Another hadith instructs leaving the doubtful for the doubt-free.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r11.claim: Repeated evil habits can corrupt the innate moral faculty until the heart is sealed, as in al-Baqara.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r11.anchor: Meğer ki şerri itiyad ede ede fıtratı tamamen bozulmuş,

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r12.claim: This passage explains the two routes in al-Balad: fujur and taqwa; guidance makes their natures clear, forbidding the former and commanding the latter.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r13.claim: Fujur precedes taqwa because preventing harm comes before securing benefit, just as cleansing comes before adornment; the aim is warning against sin and urging taqwa.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r13.anchor: hayrdan evvel zikredilmesi ise def‘-i mazarrat celb-i menfaatten akdem

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:8:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:8:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:8:anmerkung/r1.claim: Alhama means to instill (literally, to feed someone something to swallow) and is a Quranic hapax; 99:5 has similar awḥā, later a technical term for revelation.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:8:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Das Verbum ʾalhama, „eingeben“ (eigentl.: „jmd. etwas zu verschlingen geben“; vgl. WKAS, s. v. l-h-m) ist, wie Neuwirth hervorhebt, ein koranisches hapax legomenon

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:8:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:8:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:8:anmerkung/r2.claim: Fuǧūr is the verbal noun of fajara, ‘to sin’; related early forms occur in 75:5, 83:7, 82:14, and 80:42.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:8:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Fuǧūr ist den Lexika zufolge Verbalsubstantiv zu faǧara, „sündigen“

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:8:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:8:anmerkung/r3.speaker: Ahrens und Jeffery
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:8:anmerkung/r3.claim: Ahrens and Jeffery suspect Syriac-Aramaic pagrānā, ‘physical, carnal,’ influenced fuǧūr’s moral sense in an early Christian anthropology where it meant sinful.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:8:anmerkung/r3.anchor: vermuten Ahrens und Jeffery einen Einfluss von syr.-aram. pagrānā = „körperlich, fleischlich“

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:8:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:8:anmerkung/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:8:anmerkung/r4.claim: The concrete sense ‘break or cut open’ could underlie the moral sense of fuǧūr; the note on taqwā is at 92:5.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:8:anmerkung/r4.anchor: Obwohl diese moralische Verwendungsweise des Verbs durchaus von seiner konkreten Bedeutung „aufbrechen, aufschneiden“ abgeleitet werden könnte

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r1.claim: The oath’s list of opposing created phenomena moves into morality in verses 7–8 and ends with a contrastive oath naming the opposed outcomes of those moral choices.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r1.anchor: Die Liste gegensätzlicher Schöpfungsphänomene, die in V. 7.8 in den Bereich des Moralischen übergeht, endet schließlich mit einer ebenfalls kontrastiv gegliederte Schwuraussage

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p376#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p376#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p376#2/r1.claim: Qatāda says God made clear to the soul the difference between evil and piety.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p376#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فألهمها فجورها وتقواها ﴾ قال قد بين لها الفجور من التقوى

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p376#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p376#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p376#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim glosses the terms as obedience and disobedience.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p376#2/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك بن مزاحم في قوله تعالى ﴿ فألهمها فجورها وتقواها ﴾ قال الطاعة والمعصية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p488/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p488/r9.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p488/r9.claim: Ibn Jubayr glosses “inspired it” as “imposed it.”

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God made the soul know; Ibn Zayd says He explained to it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: عرفها. وقال ابن زيد: بين لها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r2.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says God enabled the soul for piety; another explanation is that He taught it and gave it power to acquire either sin or piety.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج: وفقها للتقوى، وألهمها فجورها: أي خذلها، وقيل: عرفها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī interprets inspiration of sin and piety as understanding good and evil and being enabled to choose either, supported by the agency in the next verses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ومعنى إلهام الفجور والتقوى: إفهامها وإعقالها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān calls al-Zamakhsharī’s interpretation a covert Muʿtazilite doctrine.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p139#4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p139#4/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p139#4/r8.claim: The preceding surah ended with the people of the right and left; this one summarizes the two groups in the successful purifier and failed corrupter, and its inspiration verse can explain the two paths in the previous surah.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p139#4/r8.anchor: ولما ختم سبحانه السورة المتقدمة بذكر أصحاب الميمنة وأصحاب المشأمة أعاد جل شأنه في هذه السورة الفريقين على سبيل الفذلكة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī objects to the verbal-noun reading because it would leave the following verb improperly coordinated with a noun and without an expressed or recoverable subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r1.anchor: فألهمها فجورها وتقواها وما يؤدي إليه من فساد النظم وذلك على ما في الحواشي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r2.claim: Alusi reports that the syntactic objection is answerable: earlier verbs also have implicit subjects, context licenses ellipsis, and verb-to-noun coordination is possible, though less usual.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r2.anchor: واعترض بأن الأخير منتقض بالأفعال السابقة أعني بناها طحاها سواها على أن دلالة السياق في صحة الإضمار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r3.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r3.claim: ʿAbd al-Jabbār insists that ما is a verbal noun, rejecting the relative reading because it would make God swear by created things.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r3.anchor: وأبى القاضي عبد الجبار إلا المصدرية دون المصدرية قال لما يلزم منها الأقسام بغير الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r4.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r4.claim: The Imam answers that the sun, the greatest perceptible object, is named with its signs of grandeur before God is described by three attributes, drawing the intellect beyond sensory things toward divine majesty.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r4.anchor: وأجاب عنه الإمام بأن أعظم المحسوسات الشسمس فذكرها الله تعالى مع أوصافها الدالة على عظمتها ثم ذكر ذاته المقدسة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r5.claim: Another proposal makes ما refer to the countless wise purposes in the making of heaven, spreading of earth, and shaping of the soul, with the actions and inspiration figuratively attributed to those purposes; Alusi finds this far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r5.anchor: وجوز أن تكون ما عبارة عن الأمر الذي ينيب السماء وطحيت وسويت النفس من الحكم والمصالح التي لا تحصى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r6.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses the two terms as disobedience and obedience in general, whether inward or outward.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك المعصية والطاعة مطلقا قلبيين كانا أو قالبيين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r7.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r7.claim: Mujāhid says God taught the soul to distinguish its right guidance from its error; Ibn ʿAbbās is also reported to hold this sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد تعريفهما إياها بحيث تميز رشدها ضلالها وروي ذلك عن ابن عباس كما في البحر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the verse as God making the two paths clear to the soul; Qatāda is reported with a similar explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r8.anchor: قول ابن زيد ألهمها فجورها وتقواها بينهما لها وأخرج ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وغيرهما نحوه عن قتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r9.claim: On the guidance-to-the-two-paths reading, the verse parallels the earlier statement that God showed the two ways; disobedience comes first because clearing away evil precedes adornment, or for rhyme, while another explanation sees both capacities already prepared in the soul.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r9.anchor: والآية على ذلك نظير قوله تعالى وهديناه النجدين وقدم الفجور على التقوى لأن إلهامه بهذا المعنى من مباديء تجنبه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r4.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr glosses inspiration as making something binding upon the soul.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير أنه قال في فألهمها ألزمها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r5.speaker: الواحدي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r5.claim: Al-Wāḥidī and the author of al-Muṭliʿ define inspiration as placing success or abandonment in the heart; what God places there is thereby made binding.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r5.anchor: قال الواحدي وصاحب المطلع الإلهام أن يوقع في القلب التوفيق والخذلان فإذا أوقع سبحانه في قلب عبد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r6.speaker: عمران بن حصين
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r6.claim: Two men from Muzayna ask the Prophet whether human deeds are already decreed or are a response to a prophet's proof; he answers that they are decreed, citing the soul's inspiration to sin and piety. Alusi says this need not erase any role for human capacity and choice.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r6.anchor: ويزيد ذلك قوة ما أخرجه البخاري ومسلم وأبو داود عن عمران بن حصين أن رجلين من مزينة أتيا رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p146/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146/r5.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146/r5.claim: An esoteric mapping reads the sun as the divine essence, its brightness as the Muhammadan reality, the moon as possible-being, day as the manifest world, night as contingent existence veiling the Real, heaven as intellect, earth as body, and the camel and its drink as longing and remembrance or reflection.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146/r5.anchor: وذكر بعض أهل التأويل أن الشمس إشارة إلى ذات واجب الوجود سبحانه وتعالى وضحاها إشارة إلى الحقيقة المحمدية والقمر إشارة إلى ماهية الممكن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report through Ali b. Abi Talha, says God showed the soul good and evil.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية علي بن أبي طلحة: 193/ب بين لها الخير والشر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r3.claim: In another report, Ibn Abbas says God taught the soul obedience and disobedience.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r3.anchor: وقال في رواية عطية: علمها الطاعة والمعصية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r4.speaker: الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi reports from Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas that God made the soul recognize good and what evil to avoid.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r4.anchor: وروى الكلبي عن أبي صالح عنه: عرفها ما تأتي من الخير وما تتقي [من الشر] (1)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r5.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr interprets the wording as binding the soul to its evil and piety.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r5.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: ألزمها فجورها وتقواها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r6.speaker: ابن زيد والزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says God placed both tendencies in the soul by enabling piety and abandoning it to evil; al-Zajjaj chooses this as divine enabling and withdrawal, showing that God creates piety in believers and evil in unbelievers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد: جعل فيها ذلك، يعني بتوفيقه إياها للتقوى، وخذلانه إياها للفجور

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r7.speaker: عمران بن حصين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r7.claim: Imran b. Husayn asks whether human striving follows prior decree or newly established proof; a visitor asks the Prophet and he answers that deeds are decreed, and God prepares each person for one of two abodes, citing this verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r7.anchor: عن الأسود الديلي قال: قال لي عمران بن حصين: أرأيت ما يعمل الناس

BAYDAWI-FULL:91:5-8/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:5-8/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:5-8/r4.claim: Inspiring the soul to recognize its sin and piety means explaining and defining both states or enabling it to perform them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:5-8/r4.anchor: وإلهام الفجور والتقوى إفهامهما وتعريف حالهما أو التمكين من الإتيان بهما

BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r1.claim: Biqāʿī links the two paths to the guidance of 90:10 and 76:3 and balances human acquisition with God's creation of acts in 37:96.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r2.claim: The surah's oath supports the success of those who choose guidance, exert themselves, and spend their effort, and the failure of those who follow desire.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r2.anchor: أقسم سبحانه وتعالى في هذ هالسورة على فلاح من اختيار

BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r3.claim: God inspired the soul's primordial disposition, from before the covenant, with both its rebelliousness and its piety.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r3.anchor: أي النفس إلهام الفطرة السابقة الأولى قبل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r4.claim: Fujūr is movement toward desire that breaks the bounds of revealed law; taqwā is fear that restrains the soul within those bounds.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r4.anchor: أي انبعاثها في الميل مع دواعي الشهوات وعدم الخوف

BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r5.claim: The verse uses ellipsis by pairing the mention of rebellion with the omitted opposite of restraint, and piety with the omitted absence of fear.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r5.anchor: ذكر الفجور أولا دال على السكون الذي هو ضده ثانيا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r6.claim: Inspiration means the soul was made to know and be ready for both paths; revelation and messengers then remove doubt and establish accountability.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r6.anchor: إلهامها للأمرين هو جعله لها عارفة بالخير والشر مستعدة ومتهيئة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r7.claim: Although God creates and determines the capacity and choice, actions are attributed to the soul; the outcome and decree remain hidden as a test.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p440/r7.anchor: ودل بالإضافة على أن ذلك كله منسوب إليها ومكتوب عليها وإن كان بخلقه وتقديره

DURR-FULL:v8p528/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses ‘inspired it’ as ‘taught it’ its wickedness and piety.
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس {فألهمها} قال: علمها {فجورها وتقواها}

DURR-FULL:v8p528/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r2.claim: Asked whether human deeds are already decreed or established by prophetic proof, the Prophet says they are decreed and each person is readied for one of the two abodes; he cites the verse.
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r2.anchor: عن عمران بن حصين: أن رجلا قال يا رسول الله: أرأيت ما يعمل الناس اليوم

DURR-FULL:v8p528/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet paused at the verse and prayed for his soul's piety, naming God its guardian and purifier.
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا تلا هذه الآية

DURR-FULL:v8p528/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra heard the Prophet recite the verse in prayer and ask God to grant and purify his soul.
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ {فألهمها فجورها وتقواها} قال: اللهم آت نفسي تقواها

DURR-FULL:v8p528/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Arqam says the Prophet would ask God to grant his soul piety and be its purifier and guardian.
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r5.anchor: عن زيد بن أرقم قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: اللهم آت نفسي تقواها

DURR-FULL:v8p528/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r6.claim: He glosses the oath images as the sun's light, the moon's following, daylight's illumination, night covering, and God building heaven and earth; ‘inspiring’ means showing the soul its misery.
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد {والشمس وضحاها} قال: ضوؤها {والقمر إذا تلاها} قال: تبعها

DURR-FULL:v8p529/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p529/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p529/r5.claim: God showed the soul the difference between wickedness and piety.
DURR-FULL:v8p529/r5.anchor: {فألهمها فجورها وتقواها} قال: بين لها الفجور من التقوى

DURR-FULL:v8p530/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r8.claim: He understands God's inspiration as binding wickedness and piety upon the soul.
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير {فألهمها} قال: ألزمها {فجورها وتقواها}

DURR-FULL:v8p530/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r9.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r9.claim: He glosses wickedness and piety as disobedience and obedience.
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r9.anchor: عن الضحاك {فألهمها فجورها وتقواها} قال: الطاعة والمعصية

DURR-FULL:v8p530/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r10.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r10.claim: A report contrasts the wicked soul, inspired with wickedness, with the pious soul, inspired with piety.
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r10.anchor: {فألهمها فجورها وتقواها} قال: الفاجرة ألهمها الفجور والتقية ألهمها التقوى

DURR-FULL:v8p530/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r11.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r11.claim: The report says God made guidance distinct from error and inspired each soul toward its created and decreed end.
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r11.anchor: في قوله: {فألهمها فجورها وتقواها} يقول: بين للعباد الرشد من الغي وألهم كل نفس ما خلقها له

ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r1.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r1.claim: Ibn Jubayr glosses alhamahā as making it adhere to its disposition.
ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r1.anchor: قال ابن جبير : ألزمها . وقال ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses alhamahā as making it know.
ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : عرفها . وقال ابن زيد

ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses alhamahā as making it clear to the soul.
ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r3.anchor: وقال ابن زيد : بين لها . وقال الزجاج

ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r4.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says God guides the soul to piety and abandons it with respect to wickedness.
ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج : وفقها للتقوى ،   وألهمها فجورها : أي خذلها

ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r5.claim: Another explanation says God informs the soul and gives it power to acquire either wickedness or piety.
ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r5.anchor: وقيل : عرفها وجعل لها قوة يصح معها اكتساب الفجور

ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says inspiration means understanding which path is good or bad and being empowered to choose; he cites the next verses as making the person agent of purification. Abū Ḥayyān calls this a hint of Muʿtazilism.
ABUHAYYAN:91:8/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : ومعنى إلهام الفجور والتقوى : إفهامها وإعقالها

ALUSI:91:7/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r4.speaker: الفراء والزجاج والمبرد وقتادة
ALUSI:91:7/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ, al-Zajjāj, al-Mubarrad, Qatāda and others take ما in the three parallel oath clauses as a verbal noun: building, spreading and fashioning.
ALUSI:91:7/r4.anchor: وذهب الفراء والزجاج والمبرد وقتادة وغيرهم إلى أن ما في المواضع الثلاث مصدرية أي وبنائها وطحوها وتسويتها

ALUSI:91:7/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI:91:7/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī objects that the source-noun reading disrupts the syntax of the following verb, leaving it coordinated to a noun and without an expressed or recoverable agent.

ALUSI:91:7/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:7/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī answers that an implicit agent is available from context, just as it is for the preceding verbs about building, spreading and fashioning.
ALUSI:91:7/r6.anchor: واعترض بأن الأخير منتقض بالأفعال السابقة أعني بناها طحاها سواها على أن دلالة السياق كافية في صحة الإضمار

ALUSI:91:7/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:7/r7.claim: He adds that coordinating a verb with a noun is not invalid, though less usual; the phrase can mean a soul and its fashioning, then its inspiration.
ALUSI:91:7/r7.anchor: عطف الفعل على الاسم ليس بفاسد وإن كان خلاف الظاهر

ALUSI:91:7/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:91:7/r8.claim: An objection says the فاء requires immediate sequence, while fashioning precedes the breathing of the soul and inspiration comes after maturity.
ALUSI:91:7/r8.anchor: واعترض هذا بأن الفاء يدل على الترتيب من غير مهملة والتسوية قبل نفخ الروح والإلهام بعد البلوغ

ALUSI:91:7/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:7/r9.claim: The reply defines fashioning as adjusting organs and faculties, including thought, and inspiration as showing how to use them along the two paths; this accompanies the soul from its fashioning and increases in manner as its faculties grow.
ALUSI:91:7/r9.anchor: وأجيب بأن التشوية تعديل الأعضاء والقوى ومنها المفكرة والإلهام عبارة عن بيان كيفية استعمالها في النجدين

ALUSI:91:7/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:7/r10.claim: The objection about sequence is not decisive: such ordering may be customary rather than literal, and the same objection burdens both analyses.
ALUSI:91:7/r10.anchor: على أن المهلة في نحوها عرفي وقد يعد متعقباً دون تراخ ثم أنه مشترك الإلزام

ALUSI:91:7/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r11.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI:91:7/r11.claim: Al-Ṭībī argues that the finely balanced cadence requires matching clauses and rules out coordinating the verb this way; al-Ālūsī says this assumes the following phrase is an independent sentence.
ALUSI:91:7/r11.anchor: ولا معنى لقول الطيبي النظم السري يوجب موافقة القرائن فلا يجوز ونفس وتسويتها فألهمها الله

ALUSI:91:7/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r12.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار
ALUSI:91:7/r12.claim: Al-Qāḍī ʿAbd al-Jabbār insists on the source-noun reading to avoid placing an oath by created things before God’s oath by Himself.
ALUSI:91:7/r12.anchor: وأبى القاضي عبد الجبار إلا المصدرية دون الموصولية قال لما يلزم منها تقديم الإقسام بغير الله تعالى على إقسامه

ALUSI:91:7/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r13.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI:91:7/r13.claim: Al-Imām replies that the sun, greatest among sensible things, is described first with four signs of its greatness, then God names Himself with three attributes, drawing reason from the sensible world toward divine majesty.
ALUSI:91:7/r13.anchor: وأجاب عنه الإمام بأن أعظم المحسوسات الشمس فذكرها الله تعالى مع أوصافها الأربعة الدالة على عظمها

ALUSI:91:7/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:7/r14.claim: A further possibility makes ما the cosmic order of countless wisdoms behind the sky, earth and soul, with the actions and inspiration predicated of it metaphorically; al-Ālūsī dismisses this.
ALUSI:91:7/r14.anchor: وجوز أن تكون ما عبارة عن الأمر الذي له بنيت السماء وطحيت الأرض وسويت النفس من الحكم والمصالح

ALUSI:91:7/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r15.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI:91:7/r15.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses fujūr and taqwā as disobedience and obedience generally, whether inward or outward.
ALUSI:91:7/r15.anchor: والفجور والتقوى على ما أخرج عبد بن حميد وغيره عن الضحاك المعصية والطاعة مطلقاً قلبيين كانا أو قالبيين

ALUSI:91:7/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r16.speaker: مجاهد وابن عباس
ALUSI:91:7/r16.claim: Mujāhid, also reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, explains inspiration as making the soul distinguish right guidance from error.
