ALUSI:91:7/r16.anchor: وإلهامهما النفس على ما أخرج هو وابن جرير وجماعة عن مجاهد تعريفهما إياها بحيث تميز رشدها من ضلالها وروي ذلك عن ابن عباس

ALUSI:91:7/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r17.speaker: ابن زيد وقتادة
ALUSI:91:7/r17.claim: Ibn Zayd and Qatāda give the related sense that God clarified the two tendencies to the soul.
ALUSI:91:7/r17.anchor: وقريب منه قول ابن زيد ألهمها فجورها وتقواها بينهما لها وأخرج ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وغيرهما نحوه عن قتادة

ALUSI:91:7/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:7/r18.claim: On the interpretation of inspiration as showing the two paths, the verse parallels the guidance of the two paths in Sūrat al-Balad.

ALUSI:91:7/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:7/r19.claim: Fujūr precedes taqwā because recognizing vice initiates its avoidance; clearing away evil precedes adorning the soul with good.
ALUSI:91:7/r19.anchor: وقدم الفجور على التقوى لأن إلهامه بهذا المعنى من مبادىء تجنبه وهو تخلية والتخلية مقدمة على التحلية

ALUSI:91:7/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r20.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:91:7/r20.claim: Another explanation for placing fujūr first is rhyme.

ALUSI:91:7/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r21.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:91:7/r21.claim: The possessive suffixes may indicate that the soul was already disposed to both tendencies.
ALUSI:91:7/r21.anchor: وأضيفا إلى ضمير النفس قيل إشارة إلى أن الملهم للنفس فجور وتقوى قد استعدت لهما فهما لها بحكم الاستعداد

ALUSI:91:7/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r22.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:91:7/r22.claim: The attachment of both words to the soul’s pronoun may instead serve the rhyme.

ALUSI:91:8/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r4.speaker: الفراء والزجاج والمبرد وقتادة
ALUSI:91:8/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ, al-Zajjāj, al-Mubarrad, Qatāda and others take ما in the three parallel oath clauses as a verbal noun: building, spreading and fashioning.
ALUSI:91:8/r4.anchor: وذهب الفراء والزجاج والمبرد وقتادة وغيرهم إلى أن ما في المواضع الثلاث مصدرية أي وبنائها وطحوها وتسويتها

ALUSI:91:8/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI:91:8/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī objects that the source-noun reading disrupts the syntax of the following verb, leaving it coordinated to a noun and without an expressed or recoverable agent.

ALUSI:91:8/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:8/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī answers that an implicit agent is available from context, just as it is for the preceding verbs about building, spreading and fashioning.
ALUSI:91:8/r6.anchor: واعترض بأن الأخير منتقض بالأفعال السابقة أعني بناها طحاها سواها على أن دلالة السياق كافية في صحة الإضمار

ALUSI:91:8/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:8/r7.claim: He adds that coordinating a verb with a noun is not invalid, though less usual; the phrase can mean a soul and its fashioning, then its inspiration.
ALUSI:91:8/r7.anchor: عطف الفعل على الاسم ليس بفاسد وإن كان خلاف الظاهر

ALUSI:91:8/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:91:8/r8.claim: An objection says the فاء requires immediate sequence, while fashioning precedes the breathing of the soul and inspiration comes after maturity.
ALUSI:91:8/r8.anchor: واعترض هذا بأن الفاء يدل على الترتيب من غير مهملة والتسوية قبل نفخ الروح والإلهام بعد البلوغ

ALUSI:91:8/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:8/r9.claim: The reply defines fashioning as adjusting organs and faculties, including thought, and inspiration as showing how to use them along the two paths; this accompanies the soul from its fashioning and increases in manner as its faculties grow.
ALUSI:91:8/r9.anchor: وأجيب بأن التشوية تعديل الأعضاء والقوى ومنها المفكرة والإلهام عبارة عن بيان كيفية استعمالها في النجدين

ALUSI:91:8/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:8/r10.claim: The objection about sequence is not decisive: such ordering may be customary rather than literal, and the same objection burdens both analyses.
ALUSI:91:8/r10.anchor: على أن المهلة في نحوها عرفي وقد يعد متعقباً دون تراخ ثم أنه مشترك الإلزام

ALUSI:91:8/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r11.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI:91:8/r11.claim: Al-Ṭībī argues that the finely balanced cadence requires matching clauses and rules out coordinating the verb this way; al-Ālūsī says this assumes the following phrase is an independent sentence.
ALUSI:91:8/r11.anchor: ولا معنى لقول الطيبي النظم السري يوجب موافقة القرائن فلا يجوز ونفس وتسويتها فألهمها الله

ALUSI:91:8/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r12.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار
ALUSI:91:8/r12.claim: Al-Qāḍī ʿAbd al-Jabbār insists on the source-noun reading to avoid placing an oath by created things before God’s oath by Himself.
ALUSI:91:8/r12.anchor: وأبى القاضي عبد الجبار إلا المصدرية دون الموصولية قال لما يلزم منها تقديم الإقسام بغير الله تعالى على إقسامه

ALUSI:91:8/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r13.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI:91:8/r13.claim: Al-Imām replies that the sun, greatest among sensible things, is described first with four signs of its greatness, then God names Himself with three attributes, drawing reason from the sensible world toward divine majesty.
ALUSI:91:8/r13.anchor: وأجاب عنه الإمام بأن أعظم المحسوسات الشمس فذكرها الله تعالى مع أوصافها الأربعة الدالة على عظمها

ALUSI:91:8/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:8/r14.claim: A further possibility makes ما the cosmic order of countless wisdoms behind the sky, earth and soul, with the actions and inspiration predicated of it metaphorically; al-Ālūsī dismisses this.
ALUSI:91:8/r14.anchor: وجوز أن تكون ما عبارة عن الأمر الذي له بنيت السماء وطحيت الأرض وسويت النفس من الحكم والمصالح

ALUSI:91:8/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r15.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI:91:8/r15.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses fujūr and taqwā as disobedience and obedience generally, whether inward or outward.
ALUSI:91:8/r15.anchor: والفجور والتقوى على ما أخرج عبد بن حميد وغيره عن الضحاك المعصية والطاعة مطلقاً قلبيين كانا أو قالبيين

ALUSI:91:8/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r16.speaker: مجاهد وابن عباس
ALUSI:91:8/r16.claim: Mujāhid, also reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, explains inspiration as making the soul distinguish right guidance from error.
ALUSI:91:8/r16.anchor: وإلهامهما النفس على ما أخرج هو وابن جرير وجماعة عن مجاهد تعريفهما إياها بحيث تميز رشدها من ضلالها وروي ذلك عن ابن عباس

ALUSI:91:8/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r17.speaker: ابن زيد وقتادة
ALUSI:91:8/r17.claim: Ibn Zayd and Qatāda give the related sense that God clarified the two tendencies to the soul.
ALUSI:91:8/r17.anchor: وقريب منه قول ابن زيد ألهمها فجورها وتقواها بينهما لها وأخرج ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وغيرهما نحوه عن قتادة

ALUSI:91:8/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:8/r18.claim: On the interpretation of inspiration as showing the two paths, the verse parallels the guidance of the two paths in Sūrat al-Balad.

ALUSI:91:8/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:8/r19.claim: Fujūr precedes taqwā because recognizing vice initiates its avoidance; clearing away evil precedes adorning the soul with good.
ALUSI:91:8/r19.anchor: وقدم الفجور على التقوى لأن إلهامه بهذا المعنى من مبادىء تجنبه وهو تخلية والتخلية مقدمة على التحلية

ALUSI:91:8/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r20.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:91:8/r20.claim: Another explanation for placing fujūr first is rhyme.

ALUSI:91:8/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r21.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:91:8/r21.claim: The possessive suffixes may indicate that the soul was already disposed to both tendencies.
ALUSI:91:8/r21.anchor: وأضيفا إلى ضمير النفس قيل إشارة إلى أن الملهم للنفس فجور وتقوى قد استعدت لهما فهما لها بحكم الاستعداد

ALUSI:91:8/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r22.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:91:8/r22.claim: The attachment of both words to the soul’s pronoun may instead serve the rhyme.

BAGHAWI:91:8/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:91:8/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI:91:8/r1.claim: In the narration of ʿAli ibn Abi Talha, Ibn Abbas says God made good and evil clear to the soul.
BAGHAWI:91:8/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية علي بن أبي طلحة : بين لها الخير والشر

BAGHAWI:91:8/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:91:8/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI:91:8/r2.claim: In the narration of ʿAtiyya, Ibn Abbas says God taught the soul obedience and disobedience.
BAGHAWI:91:8/r2.anchor: وقال في رواية عطية : علمها الطاعة والمعصية

BAGHAWI:91:8/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:91:8/r3.speaker: الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI:91:8/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih and Ibn Abbas, says God made known to the soul what it does and what it should avoid.
BAGHAWI:91:8/r3.anchor: وروى الكلبي عن أبي صالح عنه : عرفها ما تأتي وما تتقي

BAGHAWI:91:8/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:91:8/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI:91:8/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says God imposed its wickedness and piety upon the soul.
BAGHAWI:91:8/r4.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير : ألزمها فجورها وتقواها

BAGHAWI:91:8/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:91:8/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
BAGHAWI:91:8/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says God placed both qualities in the soul, enabling it to piety and abandoning it to wickedness.
BAGHAWI:91:8/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد : جعل فيها ذلك ، يعني بتوفيقه إياها للتقوى ، وخذلانه إياها للفجور

BAGHAWI:91:8/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:91:8/r6.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI:91:8/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers understanding inspiration as divine enabling and abandonment; this shows that God creates piety in the believer and wickedness in the unbeliever.
BAGHAWI:91:8/r6.anchor: واختار الزجاج هذا ، وحمل الإلهام على التوفيق والخذلان ، وهذا يبين أن الله عز وجل خلق في المؤمن التقوى

BAGHAWI:91:8/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:91:8/r7.speaker: الأسود الديلي عن عمران بن حصين
BAGHAWI:91:8/r7.claim: Al-Aswad al-Dayli recounts Imran ibn Husayn testing him about whether people's deeds are predestined and whether that makes punishment unjust; he answers that God owns and creates all, and Imran then cites the Prophet's answer that deeds are decreed and each person is prepared for the abode for which he was created, confirming it with this verse.
BAGHAWI:91:8/r7.anchor: عن الأسود الديلي قال : " قال لي عمران بن حصين : أرأيت ما يعمل الناس ويكادحون فيه

BAGHAWI:91:8/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:91:8/r8.speaker: جابر عن سراقة بن مالك بن جعشم
BAGHAWI:91:8/r8.claim: Jabir reports Suraqa asking the Prophet whether deeds follow already-dried decrees or future commands; the Prophet says they follow the decrees and that each person should act, since each is made easy for what he was created for.
BAGHAWI:91:8/r8.anchor: عن جابر قال : " جاء سراقة بن مالك بن جعشم فقال : يا رسول الله بين لنا ديننا

BAYDAWI:91:8/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:91:8/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:91:8/r1.claim: Ilhām here can mean explaining and making the two conditions known, or enabling the soul to perform both.
BAYDAWI:91:8/r1.anchor: وإلهام الفجور والتقوى إفهامهما وتعريف حالهما أو التمكين من الإتيان بهما

BIQAI:91:8/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:8/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:8/r1.claim: Human wrongdoing is astonishing: people knowingly pursue what harms them and fight anyone who restrains them, whereas animals avoid visible harm; reason and revelation condemn vice, while desire makes it alluring and piety difficult.
BIQAI:91:8/r1.anchor: والآدمي يقدم على ما يضره وهو يعلم ويقاتل من منعه منه

BIQAI:91:8/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:8/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:8/r2.claim: Inspiration begins with the original fitra, alluding to the primordial covenant; it means God made the soul know good and evil and ready for either.
BIQAI:91:8/r2.anchor: إلهام الفطرة السابقة الأولى قبل { ألست بربكم }[ الأعراف : 172 ]

BIQAI:91:8/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:8/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:8/r3.claim: Fujūr is the soul's rush to follow the promptings of desire without fear, breaking the boundary of the Sacred Law.
BIQAI:91:8/r3.anchor: أي انبعاثها في الميل مع دواعي الشهوات وعدم الخوف الحامل على خرق سياج الشريعة

BIQAI:91:8/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:8/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:8/r4.claim: Taqwā is fear that stills the soul and makes it protect itself with the safeguards of the Sacred Law.
BIQAI:91:8/r4.anchor: أي خوفها الذي أوجب سكونها وتحرزها بوقايات الشريعة

BIQAI:91:8/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:8/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:8/r5.claim: The verse uses iḥtibāk: mentioning vice first signals its opposite, stillness, later; mentioning piety later signals its opposite, absence of fear, earlier.
BIQAI:91:8/r5.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : ذكر الفجور أولاً دالّ على السكون الذي هو ضده ثانياً ،   وذكر التقوى ثانياً دال على ضده

BIQAI:91:8/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:8/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:8/r6.claim: Attributing both dispositions to the soul makes them its responsibility, though God creates and decrees them: He gives it power and choice for either path, explains both through scripture and messengers, and thereby establishes proof while concealing destiny and outcome.
BIQAI:91:8/r6.anchor: ودل بالإضافة على أن ذلك كله منسوب إليها ومكتوب عليها وإن كان بخلقه وتقديره لأنه أودعها قوة وجعل لها اختياراً

DURR:91:8/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:8/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR:91:8/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr glosses “inspired it” as “made it adhere.”
DURR:91:8/r1.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن سعيد بن جبير

DURR:91:8/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:8/r2.speaker: الضحاك
DURR:91:8/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses the soul’s fajūr and taqwā as disobedience and obedience.
DURR:91:8/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك { فألهمها فجورها وتقواها } قال : الطاعة والمعصية .

DURR:91:8/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:8/r3.speaker: غير مسمى
DURR:91:8/r3.claim: An unattributed report says the wicked person is inspired with wickedness and the pious person with piety.
DURR:91:8/r3.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم { فألهمها فجورها وتقواها } قال : الفاجرة ألهمها الفجور

DURR:91:8/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:8/r4.speaker: غير مسمى
DURR:91:8/r4.claim: A report says God made guidance distinct from error for people and inspired each soul with what it was created for and decreed for it.
DURR:91:8/r4.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه في قوله : { فألهمها فجورها وتقواها } يقول : بين للعباد الرشد من الغيّ

IBNASHUR:91:8/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:8/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:8/r1.claim: The clause is coordinated with sawwaha and included in the oath; the fa marks inspiration as arising from formation, and its subject refers to that formation.
IBNASHUR:91:8/r1.anchor: لأنه معطوف على صلة { ما } المصدرية ،  وعطف بالفاء لأن الإلهام ناشىء عن التسوية

IBNASHUR:91:8/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:8/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:8/r2.claim: Alternatively, ma is relative and refers to God's act: the construction, spreading, and formation that God performed.
IBNASHUR:91:8/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون { ما } موصولة صادقة على فعل الله تعالى

IBNASHUR:91:8/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:8/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:8/r3.claim: Formation reaches completion from the fetus through early childhood; physical and mental faculties develop, and inspiration follows as they mature.
IBNASHUR:91:8/r3.anchor: فالتسوية حاصلة من وقت تمام خلقة الجنين من أول أطوار الصبا إذ التسوية تعديل الخلقة

IBNASHUR:91:8/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:8/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:8/r4.claim: Ilham is a verbal noun from a causative verb; the simple verb is obsolete, and the noun is rare in Arabic with no cited pre-Islamic poetic evidence.
IBNASHUR:91:8/r4.anchor: والإِلهام :  مصدر ألهم ،  وهو فعل متعد بالهمزة ولكن المجردَ منه مُمات

IBNASHUR:91:8/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:8/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:8/r5.claim: In specialized usage ilham is knowledge arising in the self without teaching, experience, or thought, whether intuitive or reached through evidence and reasoning.
IBNASHUR:91:8/r5.anchor: ويطلق الإلهام إطلاقاً خاصاً على حدوث علم في النفس بدون تعليم ولا تجربة ولا تفكير

IBNASHUR:91:8/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:8/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:8/r6.claim: The wording is chosen to encompass all human knowledge and is a precise term for psychological meanings that the Quran revived if it did not coin it.
IBNASHUR:91:8/r6.anchor: فهذا اللفظ إن لم يكن من مبتكرات القرآن يكن مما أحياه القرآن لأنه اسم دقيق الدلالة

IBNASHUR:91:8/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:8/r7.speaker: الراغب
IBNASHUR:91:8/r7.claim: Al-Raghib defines ilham as placing something in the heart, especially when it comes from God or the higher assembly.
IBNASHUR:91:8/r7.anchor: قال الراغب :  الإلهام :  إيقاع الشيء في الروع ويختص ذلك بما كان من جهة الله تعالى وَجهة الملأ الأعلى

IBNASHUR:91:8/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:8/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:8/r8.claim: The term derives from swallowing in one gulp, while its use for knowledge without an independent basis is a Sufi technical usage.
IBNASHUR:91:8/r8.anchor: وأما إطلاق الإلهام على علم يحصل للنفس بدون مستند فهو إطلاق اصطلاحي للصوفية

IBNASHUR:91:8/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:8/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:8/r9.claim: In this verse inspiration includes primary and necessary perceptions, from an infant's instinctive search for nourishment and avoidance of harm up to the first rational acquisitions.
IBNASHUR:91:8/r9.anchor: أن من آثار تسوية النفس إدراك العلوم الأولية والإدراك الضروري المدرج ابتداء من الانسياق الجبلي نحو الأمور النافعة

IBNASHUR:91:8/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:8/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:8/r10.claim: Although revelation teaches people what vice and piety are, they could not understand divine law, accountability, or reward without the cognitive capacities God placed in them.
IBNASHUR:91:8/r10.anchor: لولا ما أودع الله في النفوس من إدراك المعلومات على اختلاف مراتبها لما فهموا ما تدعوهم إليه الشرائع الإلهية

IBNASHUR:91:8/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:8/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:8/r11.claim: Vice precedes piety because the address is to Meccan polytheists, whose deeds were mostly vice, while Muslims, marked by piety, were then few.
IBNASHUR:91:8/r11.anchor: وتقديم الفجور على التقوى مراعىً فيه أحوال المخاطبين بهذه السورة وهم المشركون ،  وأكثر أعمالهم فجور

IBNASHUR:91:8/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:8/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:8/r12.claim: The masculine grammatical attribution in alhamaha is explained by the non-literal feminine gender of taswiya's verbal noun, or by ma if it is relative.
IBNASHUR:91:8/r12.anchor: ومجيء فعل :  « ألهمها » بصيغة الإسناد إلى ضمير مذكر باعتبار أن تأنيث مصدر التسوية تأنيث غير حقيقي

IBNATIYYA:91:8/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:91:8/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:91:8/r1.claim: The fāʾ links the soul's completion in the preceding verse to this inspiration, making the inspiration its perfection.
IBNATIYYA:91:8/r1.anchor: وتسويتها إكمال عقلها ونظرها ، ولذلك ربط الكلام بقوله تعالى : { فألهمها } الآية فالفاء تعطي أن التسوية هي هذا الإلهام

IBNATIYYA:91:8/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:91:8/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:91:8/r2.claim: God made the soul recognize the paths of wickedness and piety and gave it the capacity to acquire either.
IBNATIYYA:91:8/r2.anchor: ومعنى قوله تعالى : { فجورها وتقواها } أي عرفها طرق ذلك وجعل لها قوة يصح معها اكتساب الفجور أو اكتساب التقوى

MAWARDI:91:8/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:8/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI:91:8/r1.claim: Alhama means that God taught or made the soul know.

MAWARDI:91:8/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:8/r2.speaker: ابن جبير
MAWARDI:91:8/r2.claim: Alhama means that God imposed or instilled it in the soul.

MAWARDI:91:8/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:8/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI:91:8/r3.claim: Fujūr and taqwā mean misery and happiness.

MAWARDI:91:8/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:8/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:91:8/r4.claim: Fujūr and taqwā mean evil and good.
MAWARDI:91:8/r4.anchor: الثاني : الشر والخير ، قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI:91:8/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:8/r5.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI:91:8/r5.claim: Fujūr and taqwā mean disobedience and obedience.

MAWARDI:91:8/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:8/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI:91:8/r6.claim: A further possibility is that they mean fear and hope, which impel wrongdoing and piety.
MAWARDI:91:8/r6.anchor: الرهبة والرغبة لأنهما داعيا الفجور والتقوى

MAWARDI:91:8/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:8/r7.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
MAWARDI:91:8/r7.claim: Juwaybir transmits via al-Ḍaḥḥāk from Ibn ʿAbbās that the Prophet raised his voice on reciting the verse and prayed, asking God to grant his soul piety and purify it; no grading is stated.
MAWARDI:91:8/r7.anchor: وروى جويبر عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس أن النبي عليه السلام كان إذا قرأ هذه الآية

NASAFI:91:8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:91:8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:91:8/r1.claim: God made the soul know its obedience and disobedience and understand that one is good and the other bad.
NASAFI:91:8/r1.anchor: فأعلمها طاعتها ومعصيتها أفهمها أن أحدهما حسن والآخر قبيح

QURTUBI:91:8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:8/r1.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI:91:8/r1.claim: Mujāhid, in Ibn Abī Najīḥ's report, glosses alhamahā as made it know the paths of wickedness and piety; Ibn ʿAbbās gives the same explanation.
QURTUBI:91:8/r1.anchor: أي عرفها طريق الفجور والتقوى ، وقاله ابن عباس

QURTUBI:91:8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:8/r2.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI:91:8/r2.claim: Mujāhid also explains the two terms as obedience and disobedience.
QURTUBI:91:8/r2.anchor: وعن مجاهد أيضا : عرفها الطاعة والمعصية

QURTUBI:91:8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:8/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب
QURTUBI:91:8/r3.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says that when God wills good for a servant He inspires good and the servant acts on it; when He wills harm, He inspires evil and the servant acts on it.
QURTUBI:91:8/r3.anchor: وعن محمد بن كعب قال : إذا أراد الله عز وجل بعبده خيرا

QURTUBI:91:8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:8/r4.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:91:8/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says God made the soul know the paths of good and evil, as in the two paths of al-Balad 90:10.
QURTUBI:91:8/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء : " فألهمها " قال : عرفها طريق الخير وطريق الشر

QURTUBI:91:8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:8/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:91:8/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports Ibn ʿAbbās saying that God inspires the pious believer with piety and the profligate with his wickedness.
QURTUBI:91:8/r5.anchor: وروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال : ألهم المؤمن المتقي تقواه

QURTUBI:91:8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:8/r6.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI:91:8/r6.claim: Qatāda says God made the soul's wickedness and piety clear to it.
QURTUBI:91:8/r6.anchor: وعن سعيد عن قتادة قال : بين لها فجورها وتقواها

QURTUBI:91:8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:8/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI:91:8/r7.claim: The preceding explanations have approximately the same meaning.

QURTUBI:91:8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:8/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI:91:8/r8.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet recited the verse and prayed for God to grant his soul piety and purify it, since God is the best purifier and its guardian and master.
QURTUBI:91:8/r8.anchor: وروي عن أبي هريرة قال : قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI:91:8/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:8/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:91:8/r9.claim: Juwaybir reports through al-Ḍaḥḥāk from Ibn ʿAbbās that the Prophet raised his voice while reciting the verse and prayed for his soul's piety, saying God is its guardian and best purifier.
QURTUBI:91:8/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس : أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأ

QURTUBI:91:8/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:8/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI:91:8/r10.claim: Al-fujūr and al-taqwā are verbal nouns functioning as direct objects.
QURTUBI:91:8/r10.anchor: والفجور والتقوى : مصدران في موضع المفعول به

QURTUBI:91:8/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:8/r11.speaker: عمران بن حصين
QURTUBI:91:8/r11.claim: In Muslim's report from Abū al-Aswad, ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn recounts debate over whether people's deeds are predetermined; after questioning the justice of that, Abū al-Aswad says God is not questioned, and ʿImrān explains he was testing him. Two men from Muzayna ask the Prophet the same, and he says their deeds were decreed, citing these verses as proof.
QURTUBI:91:8/r11.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم ، عن أبي الأسود الدؤلي قال : قال لي عمران بن حصين

RAZI:91:8/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:8/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:91:8/r1.claim: One view says inspiration means making the soul understand wickedness and piety, know which is good or bad, and enabling it to choose; it parallels the two paths in 90:10.
RAZI:91:8/r1.anchor: أن إلهام الفجور والتقوى ، إفهامها وإعقالهما

RAZI:91:8/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:8/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI:91:8/r2.claim: This interpretation accords with the Muʿtazilite doctrine.

RAZI:91:8/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:8/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI:91:8/r3.claim: The Muʿtazilites cite the following verse about success through purification as support for their interpretation.
RAZI:91:8/r3.anchor: قالوا : ويدل عليه قوله بعد ذلك : { قد أفلح من زكاها وقد خاب من دساها }

RAZI:91:8/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:8/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:91:8/r4.claim: The understanding-and-choice interpretation is also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās and a group of eminent exegetes.
RAZI:91:8/r4.anchor: وهذا الوجه مروي عن ابن عباس وعن جمع من أكابر المفسرين

RAZI:91:8/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:8/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:91:8/r5.claim: A second view says God inspires the believer with piety and the unbeliever with wickedness.
RAZI:91:8/r5.anchor: أنه تعالى ألهم المؤمن المتقي تقواه وألهم الكافر فجوره

RAZI:91:8/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:8/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
RAZI:91:8/r6.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr glosses the phrase as God imposing its wickedness and piety upon the soul.
RAZI:91:8/r6.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير : ألزمها فجورها وتقواها

RAZI:91:8/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:8/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
RAZI:91:8/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says God placed these qualities in the soul by granting it success in piety and abandoning it to wickedness.
RAZI:91:8/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد : جعل فيها ذلك بتوفيقه إياها للتقوى وخذلانه إياها بالفجور

RAZI:91:8/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:8/r8.speaker: الزجاج والواحدي
RAZI:91:8/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj and al-Wāḥidī choose the second interpretation.

RAZI:91:8/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:8/r9.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI:91:8/r9.claim: Al-Wāḥidī distinguishes inspiration from teaching and clarification: it is God’s placing something in the servant’s heart, thereby imposing it.
RAZI:91:8/r9.anchor: فإن الإلهام هو أن يوقع الله في قلب العبد شيئا

RAZI:91:8/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:8/r10.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI:91:8/r10.claim: Al-Wāḥidī traces ilhām to laham, to swallow or consume, and says inspiring is like delivering something into the heart.
RAZI:91:8/r10.anchor: وأصل معنى الإلهام من قولهم : لهم الشيء

RAZI:91:8/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:8/r11.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI:91:8/r11.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says Ibn Zayd’s gloss best fits the root sense and plainly means God creates piety in the believer and wickedness in the unbeliever.
RAZI:91:8/r11.anchor: فالتفسير الموافق لهذا الأصل قول ابن زيد ، وهو صريح في أن الله تعالى خلق في المؤمن تقواه

RAZI:91:8/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:8/r12.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وعطاء وعكرمة ومقاتل والكلبي
RAZI:91:8/r12.claim: They interpret the next verse to mean that the soul God purified, rectified, and cleansed prospered, that is, God enabled it to obey.
RAZI:91:8/r12.anchor: قد أفلحت وسعدت نفس زكاها الله تعالى وأصلحها وطهرها

RAZI:91:8/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:8/r13.speaker: author
RAZI:91:8/r13.claim: Earlier oaths established God’s governance of the simple and composite celestial and terrestrial bodies; inspiration now addresses the remaining question of whether voluntary animal acts also fall under His decree.
RAZI:91:8/r13.anchor: أن الآيات الثلاثة ذكرت للدلالة على كونه سبحانه مدبرا للأجسام العلوية والسفلية البسيطة والمركبة

RAZI:91:8/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:8/r14.speaker: author
RAZI:91:8/r14.claim: The verse shows that voluntary acts also come from God and His decree; everything besides God occurs under His creation and control.
RAZI:91:8/r14.anchor: بقوله : { فألهمها فجورها وتقواها } على أن ذلك أيضا منه وبه وبقضائه وقدره

RAZI:91:8/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:8/r15.speaker: author
RAZI:91:8/r15.claim: Choices must arise from an agent: if causeless, an originated thing has no maker; if caused by the servant, regress follows; if caused by God, the intended conclusion follows.
RAZI:91:8/r15.anchor: فحصولها إن كان لا عن فاعل فقد استغنى المحدث عن الفاعل ، وفيه نفي الصانع

RAZI:91:8/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:8/r16.speaker: author
RAZI:91:8/r16.claim: Introspection confirms this: an unbidden thought enters the heart, produces inclination, then bodily movement and action, proving that inspiration means divine enabling or abandonment.
RAZI:91:8/r16.anchor: فتقع صورته في قلبه دفعة ، ويترتب على وقوع تلك الصورة في القلب ميل إليه

TAB:91:8/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:8/r1.speaker: author
TAB:91:8/r1.claim: God made the soul recognize what it should do or leave, including good and evil, obedience and disobedience.
TAB:91:8/r1.anchor: وقوله :  فألهَمها فُجُورَها وتَقْوَاها يقول تعالى ذكره :  فبين لها ما ينبغي لها أن تأتي أو تذر من خير ،   أو شرّ

TAB:91:8/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:8/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:91:8/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God clarified good and evil; another report from him glosses this as teaching obedience and disobedience.
TAB:91:8/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قوله :  فأَلهَمَها فُجُورَها وَتَقْوَاها يقول :  بَيّنَ الخيرَ والشرّ .

TAB:91:8/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:8/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:91:8/r3.claim: Mujāhid explains the phrase as God making the soul know its wickedness and piety.
TAB:91:8/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح ،   عن مجاهد فأَلهَمَها فُجُورَها وَتَقْوَاها قال :  عَرّفها .

TAB:91:8/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:8/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB:91:8/r4.claim: Qatāda says God clarified the soul's wickedness and piety.
TAB:91:8/r4.anchor: عن قتادة فأَلهَمَها فُجُورَها وَتَقْوَاها :  فبَيّن لها فجورها وتقواها .

TAB:91:8/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:8/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:91:8/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses the phrase as clarifying obedience and disobedience.
TAB:91:8/r5.anchor: قال :  سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله :  فأَلهَمَها فُجُورَها وَتَقْوَاها ،   بيّن لها الطاعةَ والمعصيةَ .

TAB:91:8/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:8/r6.speaker: سفيان
TAB:91:8/r6.claim: Sufyān says God informed the soul of disobedience and obedience, and also transmits the same gloss from al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
TAB:91:8/r6.anchor: عن سفيان فأَلهَمَها فُجُورَها وَتَقْوَاها قال :  أعلمها المعصيةَ والطاعةَ .

TAB:91:8/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:8/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:91:8/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd offers a different explanation: God placed the soul's wickedness and piety within it.
TAB:91:8/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد ،   في قوله :  فأَلهَمَها فُجُورَها وَتَقْوَاها قال :  جعل فيها فجورها وتقواها .

TAB:91:8/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:8/r8.speaker: أبو الأسود الدؤلي
TAB:91:8/r8.claim: In response to ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn's question about decree and injustice, Abū al-Aswad says everything is God's creation and property, while people remain accountable.
TAB:91:8/r8.anchor: عن أبي الأسود الدّيليّ ،   قال :  قال لي عمران بن حُصَين :  أرأيت ما يعمل الناس فيه ويتكادحون

TAB:91:8/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:8/r9.speaker: عمران بن حصين
TAB:91:8/r9.claim: ʿImrān narrates that the Prophet said people's destinies were decreed, yet they should act because God prepares each person for one of two destinations, citing these verses.
TAB:91:8/r9.anchor: قال لي عمران بن حُصَين :  أرأيت ما يعمل الناس فيه ويتكادحون فيه ،   أشيء قضي عليهم

ITQAN:v2p522/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p522/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p522/r1.claim: In this phrase, hā is a feminine pronoun; elsewhere hā can be a noun of command or a particle of attention.
ITQAN:v2p522/r1.anchor: واسما ضميرا للمؤنث نحو ﴿ فألهمها فجورها وتقواها ﴾

ITQAN:v2p339/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p339/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p339/r2.claim: God’s inspiring the soul with its wickedness and piety means showing it good and evil.
ITQAN:v2p339/r2.anchor: 2094 ﴿ فألهمها فجورها وتقواها ﴾ بين الخير والشر

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r1.claim: God swears by the soul and its fashioning, then teaches it to recognize righteous and wicked deeds, a knowledge shared by ignorant and learned alike.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r1.anchor: أقسم بالنفس وخلقه لها ثم قال: فألهمها فجورها وتقواها، أي: فهمها أعمال البر وأعمال الفجور، حتى عرف ذلك الجاهل والعاقل

ALUSI:91:11/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ALUSI:91:11/r6.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr glosses God’s inspiration of the soul as making its course binding upon it; the report is transmitted by ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
ALUSI:91:11/r6.anchor: أخرج عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن سعيد بن جبير

ALUSI:91:11/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r7.speaker: أنس
ALUSI:91:11/r7.claim: Al-Daylamī also transmits this gloss from Anas as a report raised to the Prophet; no grading is stated.

ALUSI:91:11/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r8.speaker: الواحدي وصاحب المطلع
ALUSI:91:11/r8.claim: Al-Wāḥidī and the author of al-Muṭliʿ explain inspiration as placing guidance or abandonment in the heart; whichever God places is thereby made binding.
ALUSI:91:11/r8.anchor: قال الواحدي وصاحب المطلع الإلهام أن يوقع في القلب التوفيق والخذلان

ALUSI:91:11/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:91:11/r9.claim: ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn reports two men of Muzayna asking whether people’s deeds were decreed beforehand or established through prophetic teaching; the Prophet answered that they were decreed and had already passed, citing 91:7–8. The cited collections are al-Bukhārī, Muslim, and Abū Dāwūd.
ALUSI:91:11/r9.anchor: عن عمران بن حصين أن رجلين من مزينة أتيا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالا يا رسول الله
